'''Trocadero,''' also known as Troca,<ref>[http://www.trocadero.nu Trocadero.nu]</ref> is an [[apple]] and [[Orange (fruit)|orange]] flavoured [[Swedish cuisine|Swedish]] [[Soft drink|soda]] containing [[caffeine]]. It was launched in Sweden in the summer of 1953 by Saturnus AB in [[Malmö]],<ref name=":0">Trocanostalgi - [http://trocadero.nu/nostalgi/ trocadero.nu]</ref> Sweden. Trocadero has been especially popular in [[Norrland]], the northern part of Sweden, and has therefore been called the "national beverage of Norrland".<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">Saturnus AB, 06-30-2003, "Klassikern Trocadero fyller 50 år" Archived July 17, 2006 at Wayback Machine, 02-20-2008</ref>

== The name ==
Trocadero was introduced by Nils-Håkan Håkansson at Saturnus AB, and according to his grandson Edward Liepe, the name Trocadero comes from either [[Place du Trocadéro]] or Café du Trocadéro, both located in Paris, where it is pronounced with stress on the final o, but among Swedes drinking Trocadero the stress has generally been on e. However, the French name goes back to [[Isla del Trocadero]] in Spain, and in Spanish it is pronounced like in Swedish.

== History ==
The same year Trocadero was introduced, the ban of cola drinks was lifted in Sweden. Both [[Coca-Cola]] and [[Cuba Cola]] (the latter also brewed by Saturnus) were introduced to the market.<ref name=":1" /> For a long time, Trocadero was the only soda, except from cola, to contain [[caffeine]].

Saturnus eventually shifted focus and began selling essences for [[liquor]] and drink mixes. Along that line, they also began selling soda essences to other [[Brewery|breweries]] instead of producing the soda themselves. Their production of Trocadero came to an end, and in 2006 they sold the brand to NordArom AB<ref>[http://nordarom.se NordArom AB]</ref> who allowed selected breweries licensed manufacturing. Since 2017, the brand was acquired by [[Spendrups Bryggeri AB]], but Hammars Bryggeri, Mora Bryggeri and Vasa bryggeri still had licensed manufacturing until late 2017 when Spendrups was made the only licensed manufacturer.

== Other ==
Trocadero can be also found as [[bulk confectionery]]. The green and yellow bottle is made from jelly and tastes like Trocadero.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://karamellfarbrorn.se/produkt/trocadero-flaskor-5-st/|title=Karamellfarbrorn|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://varuhus1.se/trocadero-1-5kg-1|title=Varuhus1|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20161023211010/http://www.happycandy.se/trocadero-p-891.html Happy Candy] Archived from the original October 23, 2016. Three wise men (cocktail):
{{short description|Cocktail blending three types of whiskey together}}

'''Three wise men''' is a drink consisting of three types of [[Whisky|whiskey]] with brand names that are each named after a man (ordinarily [[Johnnie Walker]], [[Jack Daniel's|Jack Daniel]] and [[Jim Beam]]).<ref name="Spruce">{{cite web |first=Colleen |last=Graham |title=Three Wise Men: The Shot Drink That Mixes 3 Great Whiskies |url=https://www.thespruceeats.com/three-wise-men-shot-recipe-761509 |website=The Spruce Eats |date=September 7, 2018 |access-date=September 12, 2018}}</ref> The three named men are the "wise men" in the name of the drink, which is an allusion to the [[Biblical Magi]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Three Wise Men Recipe |url=https://bevvy.co/cocktail/three-wise-men/rcl |website=Bevvy |language=en |date=13 May 2015}}</ref> Several variations exist that include other ingredients or substitute [[tequila]] or [[rum]] for some of the whiskey.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burnett |first1=Heather |title=Three Wise Men Shot 6 Ways: The Strongest Whiskey Cocktail Ever |url=https://wordtoyourmotherblog.com/three-wise-men-shot/ |website=Word To Your Mother |date=22 April 2019}}</ref>

== Recipe ==
:1 part [[Scotch whisky]] (e.g., [[Johnnie Walker]] Red or Black Label)
:1 part [[Tennessee whiskey]] (e.g., [[Jack Daniel's]])
:1 part [[Bourbon whiskey]] (e.g., [[Jim Beam]] White or Black Label)
:Serve [[Straight up (bartending)|neat]], [[ice cube|on the rocks]], or shaken with ice and strained,<ref name="Spruce" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Three Wise Men Shot |url=https://tipsybartender.com/recipe/three-wise-men-shot/ |website=Tipsy Bartender |language=en |date=10 November 2017}}</ref> according to taste. Or serve the three whiskeys as three separate [[Shooter (drink)|shots]] that are lined up and consumed sequentially.<ref name="Spruce" />

=== Variations ===
By adding an ingredient, a number of variations can be made, such as:
* A '''three wise men go hunting''', or "three wise men on a hunt" consists of the traditional recipe with an additional 1 part [[Wild Turkey bourbon]].<ref name="Spruce" />
* A '''three wise men visit Mexico''' is made with the three aforementioned liquors and 1 part tequila, e.g., [[Jose Cuervo]].<ref name="Spruce" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Three Wise Men Shot Recipe (Quick and Easy) – Tammilee Tips |url=https://www.tammileetips.com/three-wise-men-shot-recipe/ |website=www.tammileetips.com}}</ref>

2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020201438/https://rockhillcoke.com/history/a-brief-history-of-sprite/|url-status=live}} By the 1980s, Sprite had developed a large following among teenagers. In response, Sprite began to cater to this demographic in its advertisements in 1987. "I Like the Sprite In You" was the brand's first long-running slogan, and many jingles were produced around it before its discontinuation in 1994.{{cn|date=April 2025}} [[File:Evolution of Sprite Bottles.JPG|thumb|The evolution of Sprite bottles]] In 1993, [[marketing agency]] Lowe and Partners created a new slogan, "Control your thirst" with commission from the Coca-Cola Company.{{Cite web|title=Obey Your Thirst|url=https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/sprite.html|access-date=February 23, 2021|website=pages.cs.wisc.edu|archive-date=August 12, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812192839/https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/sprite.html|url-status=live}} The new, more vibrant logo stood out more on packaging and featured a blue-to-green gradient with silver "splashes" and subtle white "bubbles" in the background. The product name, "Sprite" had a logo with a blue backdrop shadow. The words; "Great Lymon Taste!" which had been present on the previous logo, were removed. This logo was used in the United States until 2006, and similar variants were used in other countries until this year as well.{{cn|date=April 2025}} The brand's slogan was changed to "Obey Your Thirst", and jingles containing it became urban-oriented, featuring a hip-hop theme. One of the first lyrics for the new slogan was, "never forget yourself 'cause first things first, grab a cold, cold can, and obey your thirst." Under the new slogan, Sprite tapped into hip-hop culture by leveraging up and coming, as well as underground rap artists including; [[LL Cool J]], [[A Tribe Called Quest]], [[KRS-One]], [[Missy Elliott]], [[Grand Puba]], [[Common (rapper)|Common]], [[Fat Joe]], [[Nas]] and others in television commercials.{{cn|date=April 2025}} Sprite expanded its urban connections in the late 1990s by featuring both amateur and accomplished basketball players in their advertisements {{cn|date=May 2025}}. In the 1990s, one of Sprite's longest-running ad campaigns was "[[Grant Hill|Grant Hill Drinks Sprite]]" (overlapping its "Obey Your Thirst" campaign), in which the well-liked basketball player's abilities, and Sprite's importance in giving him his abilities, were humorously exaggerated.{{cite web|url=http://www.metacafe.com/watch/47179/sprite_and_its_meaning/|title=Video is temporarily not available|last=metacafe.com|access-date=March 2, 2017|archive-date=October 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030091832/http://www.metacafe.com/watch/47179/sprite_and_its_meaning|url-status=dead}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.advertisementave.com/?adid=116|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013132126/http://advertisementave.com/tv/ad.asp?adid=116|url-status=dead|title=LOTUS303 - Server Game Online Gratis Terbaik|archivedate=October 13, 2007|website=lotus303}} In 2000, Sprite commissioned graffiti artist Temper to design limited edition art,{{Cite web|title=The millionaire graffiti artist|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/birmingham/content/articles/2009/08/11/temper_feature.shtml|access-date=July 20, 2020|website=www.bbc.co.uk|language=en-gb|archive-date=March 2, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302023554/https://www.bbc.co.uk/birmingham/content/articles/2009/08/11/temper_feature.shtml|url-status=live}} which appeared on 100 million cans across Europe.{{Cite web|title=Temper|url=http://www.turnerfinearts.com/artist/temper|access-date=July 20, 2020|website=www.turnerfinearts.com|archive-date=July 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200720060258/http://www.turnerfinearts.com/artist/temper|url-status=live}} In 2004, Coke created Miles Thirst, a vinyl doll voiced by [[Reno Wilson]], used in advertising to exploit the hip-hop market for soft drinks.{{cite news | url=https://www.usatoday.com/money/advertising/adtrack/2004-04-25-sprite_x.htm | work=USA Today | first1=Theresa | last1=Howard | title=Coke creates hip-hop figure to inject Sprite with attitude | date=April 26, 2004 | access-date=September 15, 2017 | archive-date=June 24, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120624090405/http://www.usatoday.com/money/advertising/adtrack/2004-04-25-sprite_x.htm | url-status=live }} In 2006, a new Sprite logo, consisting of two yellow and green "halves" forming an "S" lemon/lime design, made its debut on Sprite bottles and cans. The slogan was changed from its long-running "Obey Your Thirst" to just "Obey" in the United States and was outright replaced with "Freedom From Thirst" in many countries. This was the decade's first major shift in advertising themes. [[File:Sprite bottle Shenzhen China.jpeg|thumb|294x294px|Chinese bottle of Sprite]] The "Sublymonal" campaign was also used as part of the [[alternate reality game]] the ''[[Lost Experience]]''.{{Cite web|url=http://www.thelostexperience.com/2006/05/10/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090315022639/http://www.thelostexperience.com/2006/05/10/|url-status=dead|title=Thelostexperience.com|archivedate=March 15, 2009|website=www.thelostexperience.com}} This also resurrected the "lymon" word. Sprite redesigned its label in 2009, removing the "S" logo.{{citation needed|date=January 2023}} In the mid-2010s, famous NBA players and hip-hop artists such as [[LeBron James]], [[Trae Young]], [[Vince Staples]], and [[Lil Yachty]] appeared in Sprite ads.{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2016/10/lil-yachty-sprite-ad-lebron-james/|title=Lil Yachty Stars in New Sprite Ad With LeBron James - XXL|date=October 12, 2016 |access-date=March 2, 2017|archive-date=March 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170315204937/http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2016/10/lil-yachty-sprite-ad-lebron-james/|url-status=live}} In July 2022, [[the Coca-Cola Company]] announced that Sprite would discontinue its green bottles on August 1 and switch to clear plastic bottles. The green plastic contains green polyethylene terephthalate (PET), an additive that cannot be recycled into new bottles.{{cite web | url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/07/27/business/sprite-green-bottle/index.html | title=Sprite will no longer be sold in green bottles | website=[[CNN]] | date=July 27, 2022 | access-date=July 28, 2022 | archive-date=August 12, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812090943/https://www.cnn.com/2022/07/27/business/sprite-green-bottle/index.html | url-status=live }} In 2022, Australia released lemon flavoured variants [[Sprite Lemon+]] and [[Sprite Lemon+|Sprite Lemon+ Zero Sugar]].{{cite news |last1=Poposki |first1=Claudia |title= Sprite releases two new flavours with a caffeine twist |url=https://www.news.com.au/lifestyle/food/drink/sprite-releases-two-new-flavours-with-a-caffeine-twist/news-story/09453f01c4b86251bf84991d75635f06 |access-date=September 5, 2022 |publisher=[[news.com.au]] |date=October 3, 2022}} In 2024, Sprite-mint was made available in some select Asian markets.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-12 |title=Coca-Cola Launches Sprite Lemon Mint in Bangladesh Amid Acquisition Deal |url=https://econotimes.com/Coca-Cola-Launches-Sprite-Lemon-Mint-in-Bangladesh-Amid-Acquisition-Deal-1673310 |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=EconoTimes |language=en}} ===Formula changes=== In France in 2012, the drink was reformulated removing 30% of the sugar and replacing it with the sweetener [[stevia]],{{cite web |url=http://www.coca-cola.co.uk/health/introducing-stevia-sweetener.html |title=Stevia Sweetener UK: The New Zero-Calorie Sweetener From Natural Origins - Coca-Cola GB |publisher=Coca-cola.co.uk |date=April 13, 2010 |access-date=November 7, 2013 |archive-date=March 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150330114808/http://www.coca-cola.co.uk/health/introducing-stevia-sweetener.html |url-status=dead }} leading to the drink containing fewer calories. This soon spread to Ireland, the UK, the Netherlands and Poland in 2013.{{cite web |url=http://www.distrifood.nl/Fabrikanten/Algemeen/2013/7/Coca-Cola-Sprite-eerste-drank-met-stevia-1299048W/ |title=Coca-Cola: Sprite eerste drank met stevia (Dutch) |publisher=Distrifood.nl |date=July 2, 2013 |access-date=June 16, 2014 |archive-date=July 7, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707004257/http://www.distrifood.nl/Fabrikanten/Algemeen/2013/7/Coca-Cola-Sprite-eerste-drank-met-stevia-1299048W/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite web | url=https://www.rp.pl/biznes/art12779561-sprite-w-polsce-tylko-ze-stewia | title=Sprite w Polsce tylko ze stewią }} A further formula change happened in the UK in 2018. This formula change, done to coincide with the [[sugary drinks tax]] in the country, reduces the sugar amount and replaces stevia with [[aspartame]] and [[acesulfame K]].{{cite web |author1=Arthur, Rachel |title=Sprite reduces sugar but ditches stevia, citing best taste for lower sugar UK recipe |url=https://www.beveragedaily.com/Article/2018/03/08/Sprite-reduces-calories-but-ditches-stevia-citing-best-taste-for-lower-sugar-UK-recipe |website=Beverage Daily |access-date=July 28, 2018 |date=March 8, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129013950/https://www.beveragedaily.com/Article/2018/03/08/Sprite-reduces-calories-but-ditches-stevia-citing-best-taste-for-lower-sugar-UK-recipe |url-status=live }} This formula was later extended to other regions across the world to coincide with similar sugar tax rules. In the Netherlands in March 2017, Coca-Cola announced that Sprite would be relaunched exclusively as a sugar-free drink, with the standard variety being discontinued and Sprite Zero being renamed as simply Sprite.{{cite web | url=https://www.retaildetail.eu/news/food/sprite-zero-will-become-sprite-netherlands/ | title=Sprite Zero will become Sprite in the Netherlands | date=March 10, 2017 }} This change was expanded to Ireland in 2018.{{cite web|title=Sprite Goes No Sugar|url=https://ie.coca-colahellenic.com/en/our-stories/sprite-goes-no-sugar/|date=April 23, 2018|access-date=April 4, 2019|archive-date=April 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404171611/https://ie.coca-colahellenic.com/en/our-stories/sprite-goes-no-sugar/|url-status=dead}} In Australia, Sprite was relaunched with a new recipe containing 40% less sugar (compared with old Sprite) in August 2019. Unlike most of the reformulations this version does not use aspartame, instead using [[sucralose]] in addition to acesulfame K.{{Cite web|url=https://www.coca-colacompany.com/au/brands/sprite|title=Sprite Varieties - Classic & No Sugar | Coca-Cola Australia|access-date=January 16, 2021|archive-date=October 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026223150/https://www.coca-colacompany.com/au/brands/sprite|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |title=Fanta and Sprite join the No Sugar Movement |url=https://www.coca-colacompany.com/au/news/fanta-and-sprite-join-the-no-sugar-movement |access-date=August 29, 2022 |website=www.coca-colacompany.com |language=en-AU |archive-date=June 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610235317/https://www.coca-colacompany.com/au/news/fanta-and-sprite-join-the-no-sugar-movement |url-status=live }} In March 2023, Coca-Cola announced another further formula change for Sprite and Sprite Zero Sugar in the United Kingdom, produced to differentiate the two varieties. The new formula has slightly increased sugar content but still contains aspartame and acesulfame K.{{cite web | url=https://www.coca-cola.co.uk/our-business/media-centre/sprite-unveils-a-new--irresistible--taste-and-striking-new-look | title=SPRITE UNVEILS A NEW 'IRRESISTIBLE' TASTE AND STRIKING NEW LOOK }} Some territories including France, Poland and Germany use a similar lower-sugar formula but do not utilize any artificial sweeteners. '''Wanna Sprite Cranberry?''' In mid-November 2017, Sprite released an ad for the Sprite Cranberry variation, featuring [[LeBron James]] and rapper [[DRAM (musician)|DRAM]]. The ad is animated in a style reminiscent of [[Rankin/Bass Animated Entertainment|Rankin-Bass]] holiday specials such as [[Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (TV special)|''Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer'']], and features a rambunctious family gathering during the holidays as LeBron enters saying "Wanna Sprite Cranberry?".{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.ispot.tv/ad/wMzg/sprite-cranberry-cranberry-animated-featuring-lebron-james |title=Sprite Cranberry TV Spot, 'Cranberry Animated' Featuring LeBron James |language=en |access-date=2024-10-28 |via=www.ispot.tv}} The commercial gained popularity on various sites for its meme potential, in particular the "Wanna Sprite Cranberry" line delivery and LeBron as he is portrayed in the ad were commonly associated with meme culture around the holidays as the commercial aired and re-aired yearly.{{Cite web |date=2017-12-19 |title=Wanna Sprite Cranberry |url=https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/wanna-sprite-cranberry |access-date=2024-10-28 |website=Know Your Meme |language=en}} The commercial was even edited by The Coca-Cola Company to feature Winter Spice Cranberry, the replacement for Sprite Cranberry, once Sprite Cranberry was phased out.{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.ispot.tv/ad/tr_t/sprite-winter-spiced-cranberry-the-thirstiest-time-of-the-year-feat-lebron-james |title=Sprite Winter Spiced Cranberry TV Spot, 'The Thirstiest Time of the Year' Feat. Test pilot (cocktail):
{{short description|Type of cocktail}}
The '''test pilot''' cocktail is a vintage [[Tiki culture|tiki drink]] invented by Donn Beach. Beach was known for changing his recipes over time,<ref>{{cite web |title=Jet Pilot soars over its ancestors |url=http://www.slammie.com/atomicgrog/blog/2012/02/07/mai-kai-cocktail-review-jet-pilot-soars-over-its-ancestors-with-flying-colors/ |website=slammie.com |date=7 February 2012 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref> and multiple versions of the test pilot attributed to both him and others make the cocktail one of his more frequently imitated and varied tiki drinks.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Berry |first1=Jeff |title=Beachbum Berry Remixed |date=2010 |publisher=Club Tiki Press |location=San Jose|page=96 }}</ref> Test pilot recipes call for multiple rums and typically include the use of [[falernum]] syrup and lime juice. The more popular also include Pernod ([[pastis]]/[[absinthe]]) and [[bitters]].

==Test pilot versions==
A recipe from a [[Don the Beachcomber]] drink guide calls for 1 oz of Lemon Hart Demerara 151 proof rum and 3/4 oz each of Jamaican dark rum, Puerto Rican dark rum, lime juice, grape juice, and honey. Two dashes each of bitters and grenadine should also be added, then flash blended with cracked ice and served in a double [[old fashioned glass]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bitner |first1=Arnold |title=Hawai'i Tropical Rum Drinks by Don the Beaschcomber |date=2001 |publisher=Mutual Publishing |location=Honolulu|page=47}}</ref> The date of the recipe's origin and when and where it was served is not mentioned.

Another version that Jeff Berry attributes to Donn Beach from circa 1941 while less strong is still very potent and calls for 1 1/2 oz of Jamaican dark rum, 3/4 oz of Puerto Rican light rum, 3 teaspoons of [[Cointreau]], 1/8 a teaspoon of Pernod, a 1/2 oz of both lime juice and falernum syrup, and a dash of bitters.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Berry |first1=Jeff |title=Beachbum Berry Remixed |date=2010 |publisher=Club Tiki Press |location=San Jose|page=96 }}</ref> The use of Pernod and bitters was employed by Beach as one of his signature combinations, and some cocktail enthusiasts feel it is a pivotal part of the recipe.<ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot |url=http://www.cocktailchronicles.com/2006/08/01/test-pilot/ |website=cocktailchronicles.com |date=August 2006 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Classic Tiki - The Jet Pilot |url=https://cold-glass.com/2016/06/05/classic-tiki-the-jet-pilot/ |website=cold-glass.com |date=5 June 2016 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot Tiki Drink Recipe |url=https://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2011/04/test-pilot-tiki-drink-recipe.html |website=seriouseats.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref> Several additional cocktail recipe references choose to highlight this version.<ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot Cocktail Recipe |url=https://tuxedono2.com/test-pilot-cocktail-recipe |website=tuxedono2.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot |url=https://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/test-pilot |website=myrecipes.com |accessdate=19 February 2019 |archive-date=3 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190303201505/https://www.myrecipes.com/recipe/test-pilot |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot Recipe |url=https://www.supercall.com/recipe/test-pilot-recipe |website=supercall.com |date=9 August 2016 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot |url=https://kindredcocktails.com/cocktail/test-pilot |website=kindredcocktails.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref>

A [[Trader Vic's|Trader Vic]] test pilot version listed in his 1972 revised drink guide switches the lime juice for lemon and jettisons the Pernod and bitters, calling only for 1 3/4 oz dark Jamaican rum, 3/4 oz light Puerto Rican rum, 1/4 oz of Cointreau, 1/4 oz falernum, and 1/4 oz lemon juice.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Vic |first1=Trader |title=Trader Vic's Bartenders Guide, Revised |date=1972 |publisher=[[Doubleday (publisher)|Doubleday]] |location=Garden City, NY |edition=revised|page=186}}</ref>  ''Difford's Guide'' chose to highlight the Trader Vic's version.<ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot |url=https://www.diffordsguide.com/cocktails/recipe/1940/test-pilot |website=diffordsguide.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref>

==The Jet Pilot==
Some Beachcomber and Trader Vic competitors named their versions as the ''Jet Pilot'', including at [[Joseph Stephen Crane|The Luau]] restaurant and the [[Mai-Kai Restaurant|Mai-Kai]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pilot Tiki Cocktails |url=https://blog.distiller.com/pilot-tiki-cocktails/ |website=blog.distiller.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Classic Tiki - The Jet Pilot |url=https://cold-glass.com/2016/06/05/classic-tiki-the-jet-pilot/ |website=cold-glass.com |date=5 June 2016 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref> The Jet Pilot was similar to Beach's 1941 version but was slightly spicier with the addition of stronger rum, grapefruit juice, and cinnamon syrup.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tiki Classics Jet Pilot |url=http://cocktailchem.blogspot.com/2011/12/tiki-classics-jet-pilot.html |website=cocktailchem.blogspot.com |date=6 December 2011 |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Jet Pilot Cocktail Recipe |url=https://www.thespruceeats.com/jet-pilot-cocktail-recipe-760532 |website=thespruceeats.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref>

==Impact on tiki culture==
Beyond the Jet Pilot, other aviation themed tiki cocktails include the similarly named ''Ace Pilot'', Don Beach's [[Q.B. Cooler]], and Trader Vic's [[PB2Y (cocktail)|PB2Y]] (named after the Navy's [[Consolidated PB2Y Coronado|Coronado plane]]).

A [[tiki bar]] named ''Test Pilot'' operates in [[Santa Barbara, California]], that serves a test pilot cocktail, described as having a flavor profile of "house rum blend, clove, citrus, bitters, [and] absinthe foam".<ref>{{cite web |title=Test Pilot |url=http://www.testpilotcocktails.com/ |website=testpilotcocktails.com |accessdate=19 February 2019}}</ref>

'''Starry''' is a [[lemon-lime soft drink]] created by [[PepsiCo]]. Distribution began in January 2023. The brand is aimed at competing against [[the Coca-Cola Company]]'s [[Sprite (drink)|Sprite]]. In January 2023, Starry replaced [[Sierra Mist]] as Pepsi's lemon-lime flavored drink, in part because Sierra Mist failed to gain market share in the growing category of lemon-lime drinks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simauchi |first=Kevin |date=2023-01-11 |title=PepsiCo ends Sierra Mist, launches Starry to take on Sprite |url=https://www.staradvertiser.com/2023/01/11/breaking-news/pepsico-ends-sierra-mist-launches-starry-to-take-on-sprite/ |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=Honolulu Star-Advertiser |language=en-US |archive-date=January 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116094058/https://www.staradvertiser.com/2023/01/11/breaking-news/pepsico-ends-sierra-mist-launches-starry-to-take-on-sprite/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Snider |first=Mike |date=January 13, 2023 |title=Goodbye, Sierra Mist. Hello to Starry, Pepsi's new lemon-lime soda to take on Sprite |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/food/2023/01/13/starry-pop-pepsis-lemon-lime-soda/11046280002/ |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |archive-date=January 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116095314/https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/food/2023/01/13/starry-pop-pepsis-lemon-lime-soda/11046280002/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Starry contains no [[caffeine]], and as of April 2023, is available in Regular and Zero-Sugar varieties.

==History==
In July 2022, food blogger SodaSeekers reported that PepsiCo purchased a domain name for a new brand of lemon-lime drink that would eventually replace [[Sierra Mist]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanchez |first=Rudy |date=October 13, 2022 |title=PepsiCo Launches Starry, A New Lemon-Lime Soda For the Kids, AKA, Gen Z |url=https://www.thedieline.com/blog/2022/10/13/pepsico-launches-starry-a-new-lemon-lime-soda-for-the-kids-aka-gen-z |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=Dieline |language=en |archive-date=March 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314180930/https://www.thedieline.com/blog/2022/10/13/pepsico-launches-starry-a-new-lemon-lime-soda-for-the-kids-aka-gen-z |url-status=live }}</ref> The following month, in August 2022, the company filed for a trademark for the brand name Starry as well as for a logo.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starry Lemon Lime – Trademark Application of Portfolio Concentrate Solutions Unlimited Company – Serial Number 97534420 |url=http://trademarks.justia.com/975/34/starry-lemon-97534420.html |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=trademarks.justia.com |language=en |archive-date=March 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230301225643/https://trademarks.justia.com/975/34/starry-lemon-97534420.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The brand began being distributed in stores in January 2023 with marketing geared towards [[Generation Z]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Springer |first=Jon |date=January 6, 2023 |title=Pepsico to Launch New Sprite Competition to Target Gen Z |url=https://adage.com/article/marketing-news-strategy/pepsico-launch-lemon-lime-soda-starry-target-gen-z/2462021 |work=Ad Age |access-date=January 7, 2023 |archive-date=January 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230113214155/https://adage.com/article/marketing-news-strategy/pepsico-launch-lemon-lime-soda-starry-target-gen-z/2462021 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=PepsiCo Partners |url=https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/PEPSICO-BRANDS/STARRY/c/brand_starry?source=brand_pepsicobrands&root=beverages&selectedBrand=brand_starry |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=www.pepsicopartners.com |archive-date=January 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230107034429/https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/PEPSICO-BRANDS/STARRY/c/brand_starry?source=brand_pepsicobrands&root=beverages&selectedBrand=brand_starry |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Bloomberg Businessweek]]'' reported industry analysts suggested a successful campaign to grab market share could mean taking 5–10% market share away from Sprite.<ref name="bb202304">{{Cite web |last=Pulley |first=Brett |date=2023-04-21 |title=Sprite Is So Popular That Pepsi Launched a New Lemon-Lime War |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-04-21/pepsi-s-starry-aims-to-steal-share-from-coke-s-sprite |access-date=2023-04-29 |website=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |language=en |archive-date=April 24, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424034319/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-04-21/pepsi-s-starry-aims-to-steal-share-from-coke-s-sprite |url-status=live }}</ref>

Starry is sold in cans in sizes of either {{convert|7.5|usoz}} or {{convert|12|usoz}}, and in plastic bottles with sizes including {{convert|16|usoz}}, 500 ml, and two liters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Soft Drinks {{!}} Beverages |url=https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/BEVERAGES/Soft-Drinks/c/softDrinks?q=:relevance:displayCategory:true:locationAvailibility:true:brand:brand_starry&showProductListing=true&text=&productType= |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=www.pepsicopartners.com |archive-date=January 14, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230114182145/https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/BEVERAGES/Soft-Drinks/c/softDrinks?q=:relevance:displayCategory:true:locationAvailibility:true:brand:brand_starry&showProductListing=true&text=&productType= |url-status=live }}</ref> Its syrup is also available in [[SodaStream]] devices.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Facts About Your Favorite Foods and Beverages (U.S.) {{!}} Starry SodaStream - 14.9 fl oz |url=https://www.pepsicoproductfacts.com/Home/product?formula=F0000014673&form=RTD&size=14.9 |access-date=2025-06-03 |website=www.pepsicoproductfacts.com}}</ref> Since its inception, Starry has been composed of carbonated water, [[high-fructose corn syrup]], [[citric acid]], natural flavor, and various preservatives.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Starry |url=https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/PEPSICO-BRANDS/STARRY%E2%84%A2/STARRY/Starry/p/1-15HETN-1 |access-date=2023-01-14 |website=www.pepsicopartners.com |archive-date=January 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130051718/https://www.pepsicopartners.com/pepsico/en/USD/PEPSICO-BRANDS/STARRY%E2%84%A2/STARRY/Starry/p/1-15HETN-1 |url-status=live }}</ref> Sierra Mist was sweetened using cane sugar before it was discontinued.<ref name="delish202304">{{Cite web |last=Romero |first=Gabby |date=2023-04-14 |title=We Taste-Tested Starry And Sierra Mist To See If They're Actually Different |url=https://www.delish.com/food-news/a43592446/starry-sierra-mist-comparison/ |access-date=2023-04-29 |website=Delish |language=en-us |archive-date=April 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230429183157/https://www.delish.com/food-news/a43592446/starry-sierra-mist-comparison/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Starry has been the official soft drink of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]], and [[NBA G League]] since 2023. The spokespeople for the brand have been basketball stars [[Zion Williamson]], [[Zach LaVine]], [[Klay Thompson]], [[A'ja Wilson]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=PepsiCo’s new Starry brand named official soft drink of NBA, WNBA {{!}} Marketing Dive |url=https://www.marketingdive.com/news/pepsico-starry-NBA-marketing-sponsor-all-star-weekend/641733/ |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=www.marketingdive.com |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obias |first=Rudie |date=2024-02-15 |title=NBA Star Giannis Antetokounmpo Teams Up With Starry Soda for New Commercial Ahead of All-Star Weekend |url=https://variety.com/2024/shopping/news/starry-giannis-antetokounmpo-where-to-buy-1235912199/ |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

Since the 2022–23 NBA season, Starry has been the sponsor of the annual [[Three-Point Contest]] as a part of [[NBA All-Star weekend|All-Star weekend]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=Brian |title=All-Star 2023: Starry 3-Point Contest brings new twists |url=https://www.nba.com/news/all-star-2023-3-point-contest-analysis |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206115907/https://www.nba.com/news/all-star-2023-3-point-contest-analysis |archive-date=February 6, 2024 |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> The sponsorship includes naming rights for the contest as well as two special "Starry Range" shot balls placed {{convert|6|ft|spell=in}} behind the [[3 point line|3-point line]]. This partnership replaces [[Mountain Dew]] as the event's previous sponsor and "DEW Zone" as the special shot balls used during the contest.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kidane |first=Benyam |date=2023-02-18 |title=What is Starry Range? NBA All-Star 3-Point Contest adds special long-distance shots |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/starry-range-nba-all-star-3-point-contest/xtluyan2njxzogbkwb2dxuq9 |access-date=2024-02-06 |website=Sporting News |language=en-us}}</ref>

Тархуна | image = 龙蒿汽水.jpg | caption = Bottled Tarkhuna by ''Natakhtari'' | type = [[Soft drink]] | origin = [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] | introduced = {{Start date and age|1887}} | color = [[Green]] | flavor = [[Tarragon]] and [[Galium odoratum|woodruff]] }} {{Georgian cuisine}} '''Tarkhuna''' ({{lang-ka|ტარხუნა}}, {{IPA|ka|tʼaɾχuna}}; {{Langx|ru|Тархуна}}) is a [[Georgian cuisine|Georgian]][https://books.google.com/books?id=3PM_FnWgPBAC&q=tarragon+tarkhuna+&pg=PA43 The Georgian Feast by Darra Goldstein p.43, University of California Press, 1999] carbonated [[tarragon]] and/or [[Galium odoratum|woodruff]]-flavored [[soft drink]], first ever created in 1887 in [[Kutaisi]] by Georgian pharmacist Mitrofan Lagidze. Mitrofan Lagidze began to add odorous chukhpuch containing extract of Caucasian tarragon to sparkling water with natural syrups of his own production.{{Cite web |title=This Bright Green Tarragon Soda Was a Soviet Summer Treat |url=https://www.atlasobscura.com/foods/georgian-tarragon-soda-tarkhuna |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Atlas Obscura |language=en}} Before the First World War, Lagidze repeatedly received gold medals at international exhibitions for his water.{{Cite web |title=Lagidze Water - Manufacturer - Needl by Wabel |url=https://needl.co/company/lagidze/ |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=needl. |language=en-US}} In 1927, the Soviet authorities built a plant for the production of "[[Lagidze water]]" in [[Tbilisi]], and Lagidze himself was appointed director. ==Availability== As of 2019, Tarkhuna is produced in Georgia by multiple brands including Natakhtari, Zedazeni and Lagidze, in Lithuania by Selita Klasika as ''Tarchunas'' and in Russia, where one of the producers is OAO Narzan under the brand Ledyanaya Zhemjushina. The drink became available on the general [[USSR]] market for the first time in 1981. The pilot batch was sold on the territory of the [[Moscow Botanical Garden of Academy of Sciences| Main Botanical Garden of the USSR Academy of Sciences]] in standard 0.33 liter bottles. Subsequently, its recipe was transferred to food industry enterprises, and, since 1983, "Tarhun" began to be sold in many republics of the USSR and administrative regions of the [[RSFSR]] in bottles of 0.33 and 0.5 liters. == Trademark status == In a trademark dispute between OÜ Acerra and AS Tallinna Karastusjoogid, the Estonian [[Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications]] determined that the word ''Tarhun'' is a descriptive term for the drink, and is thus not trademarkable under the laws of the [[Republic of Estonia]].{{cite web |title=ruling 808-o |work=Majandus- ja Kommunikatsiooniministeeriumi Tööstusomandi Apellatsioonikomisjon |publisher=Majandus- ja Kommunikatsiooniministeerium |date=28 April 2006 |url=http://www.mkm.ee/failid/808_o.pdf |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091229072638/http://www.mkm.ee/failid/808_o.pdf |archivedate=29 December 2009}} In Estonia, it was possible to find both the Estonian-made and Russian-made Tarhun drinks from the same soft drinks aisle, as the soft drink is distilled and bottled in both countries, though by different companies and with slightly different recipes. In 2015, the Estonian soft drinks company AS Tallinna Karastusjoogid, who were the local producer and distributor of "Tarhun", ceased operations, and its owner AS Haljas put the producer on sale to a 'foreign investor', whose name and country of origin has remained unknown.{{cite news |last=Gamzejev |first=Erik |title=Jõhvi joogitehas võib taas tööle hakata |language=Estonian |trans-title=The Jõhvi drinks factory might start working again |publisher=[[Põhjarannik]] |date=2015-03-20 |url=http://pr.pohjarannik.ee/?p=12846 |url-status=dead |archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20170728085710/http://pr.pohjarannik.ee/?p=12846 |archivedate=2017-07-28}} As of 2019, stores in Estonia variously sell tarkhuna lemonades made in Georgia, Lithuania, and Russia; though none of these tarkhuna brands has reached universal distribution across most store chains. == See also == * [[Duchess (drink)]] * [[Lagidze water]] == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Soft drinks]] [[Category:Georgian drinks]] [[Category:Russian drinks]] [[Category:1887 introductions]]

A '''sour''' is a traditional family of [[mixed drink]]s. ''Sours'' belong to one of the old families of original cocktails and are described by [[Jerry Thomas (bartender)|Jerry Thomas]] in his 1862 book ''How to Mix Drinks''.<ref name="Cocktail Chronicles">Paul Clarke. [http://www.cocktailchronicles.com/2005/09/25/make-yourself-comfortable/ Make Yourself Comfortable]. September 25, 2005. The Cocktail Chronicles. Retrieved on January 1, 2007.</ref> 

Sours are mixed drinks containing a base liquor, [[Lemon juice|lemon]] or [[lime juice]], and a sweetener ([[simple syrup]] or [[orgeat syrup]]).<ref name="Joy 158-159">{{cite book|author=Regan, Gary |title=The Joy of Mixology, The Consummate Guide to the Bartender's Craft |year=2003 |publisher=Clarkson Potter |isbn=0609608843|pages=158–159}}</ref> [[Egg white|Egg whites]] are also included in some sours.

==Types of sours==

===Gin sour===
The '''gin sour''' is a traditional [[mixed cocktail]] that predates [[Prohibition in the United States]]. It is a simple combination of gin, lemon juice, and sugar. Adding carbonated water to this turns it into a [[gin fizz]].

It was popular during the 1940s, and [[Kevin Starr]] includes it in "an array of drinks (the gin sour, the whiskey sour, the [[Rickey (cocktail)#The gin Rickey|gin Rickey]], the [[Tom Collins]], the [[Pink lady (cocktail)|pink lady]], the [[Old fashioned (cocktail)|old fashioned]]) that now seem period pieces, evocative of another era".{{ref|starr}}

===Pisco sour===
{{main|Pisco sour}}
The classic '''pisco sour''' recipe contains [[pisco]] brandy (usually an un-aged grape brandy from Perú), fresh lime juice, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup, egg white, and [[bitters]].<ref name="LA Speakeasy">Navarro, V. [https://www.laspeakeasy.com/pisco-sour/ Classic Pisco Sour] ''LA Speakeasy''</ref> It is [[Cocktail shaker|shaken]], [[Cocktail strainer|strained]], and served [[Straight up (bartending)|straight]] in a cocktail glass then garnished with the bitters (cinnamon can be used). The addition of egg white creates a foamy head when shaken before serving. While pisco sour is flavoured with key lime by default, pisco is combined with other fruit to create mango sour, maracuya ([[passion fruit]]) sour, lucuma sour and so forth.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://peru.com/estilo-de-vida/gastronomia/maracuya-sour-que-necesitas-y-como-se-prepara-este-exquisito-trago-noticia-213918 |title=Maracuya sour: Qué necesitas y cómo se prepara este exquisito trago |first=Redacción |last=Peru.com |date=December 6, 2013 |website=Perú.com}}</ref> Peru has a National Pisco Sour Day (which lasts a weekend) in mid-February,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://elcomercio.pe/noticias/dia-del-pisco-sour |title=Todas las noticias de Día del Pisco Sour |website=El Comercio}}</ref> and Chile has Pisco Day in mid-May.

===Rum sour===

The basic [[Daiquiri]], sometimes called a Daiquiri sour, is made with rum, lime juice and simple syrup.<ref>{{cite web |title=Daiquiri cocktail |website=Difford's |url=https://www.diffordsguide.com/g/1083/daiquiri-cocktail}}</ref> One account of the drink's origin is that the general manager of the Spanish-American Iron Core Company, which operated the "Daiquiri" mine, ran out of gin one night when making gin sour for his guests, and switched to rum. This rum sour became known as the Daiquiri. However, earlier printed recipes for rum sour exist such as one from [[Jerry Thomas (bartender)|Jerry Thomas]] from 1887.<ref>{{cite book |last=Broom |first=Dave |title=Rum The Manual |date=2016 |publisher=Octopus Books |isbn=9781784720667 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HfwyDQAAQBAJ}}</ref>

===Whiskey sour===

{{main|Whiskey sour}}

The '''whiskey sour''' is a [[mixed drink]] containing [[bourbon whiskey]] or [[rye whiskey]], lemon juice, sugar, and optionally a dash of egg white to make it a Boston Sour. It is shaken and served either straight or over ice. The traditional garnish is half an orange slice and a [[maraschino cherry]]. If floated with claret red wine it's called a [[New York sour]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Difford |first=Simon |title=New York Sour |url=https://www.diffordsguide.com/cocktails/recipe/3398/new-york-sour-cocktail |access-date=September 29, 2022 |website=Diffords Guide}}</ref>

A notable variant of the whiskey sour is the [[Ward 8 (cocktail)|Ward 8]], which often is based with either bourbon or rye whiskey, both lemon and orange juices, and grenadine syrup as the sweetener. The egg white sometimes employed in other whiskey sours is generally not included in this variation.

===Other sours===
* '''[[Amaretto sour]]''': [[Amaretto]] liqueur, lemon juice and sometimes egg white, bitters or sugar syrup.<ref>{{cite web|title=Amaretto Sour|url=https://www.diffordsguide.com/cocktails/recipe/53/amaretto-sour|website=Difford's Guide|access-date=21 March 2018}}</ref>
* '''Brandy sour''' or [[brandy daisy]] (Jerry Thomas, 1887): brandy, clear or orange [[curaçao liqueur|curaçao]], sugar, lemon juice, shaken and strained into a wine glass.
* '''[[Caipirinha]]''': [[Cachaça]], sugar, lime, ice in an [[old fashioned glass]].
* '''[[Brandy sour (Cyprus)|Cypriot brandy sour]]''': [[Cyprus brandy]], lemon cordial and bitters, stirred in a tall glass, and topped with soda or lemonade.
* '''[[b:Bartending/Cocktails/Glossary#M|Midori sour]]''': Honeydew melon liquor, grenadine, lemon juice. Poured properly, it resembles a green [[Tequila sunrise (cocktail)|tequila sunrise]] with visible layers.
* '''Santa Cruz sour''' (Jerry Thomas, 1887): Santa Cruz rum, sugar, lemon juice, shaken and strained into a wine glass.
* '''Tequila sour''': Tequila, lemon juice, lime juice, agave nectar, Bittercube Corazon bitters, egg white.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tequila Sour|url=http://recipe.awesomedrinks.com/recipe/tequila-sour/|website=Awesome Drinks}}</ref>

Tom and Jerry (mixed drink):
{{short description|Christmas-time cocktail in the United States}}
{{Infobox drink
| name        = Tom and Jerry
| image       = Tom & Jerry as served at Karl Ratzsch's, Milwaukee.jpg  
| caption     = A Tom & Jerry cocktail 
| type        = [[List of cocktails|Cocktail]]
| base        = 
| ingredients ={{plainlist|Eggs or egg whites, powdered sugar, brandy, rum}}
| served      = Hot in a mug or bowl
| prep        = Separate eggs. Beat egg whites until stiff. Mix egg yolks with powdered sugar. Put a spoonful of yolk mixture in cup, and mix with brandy and rum. Fold in some egg white, then add hot milk and top with more egg white. Stir gently to fold in the egg white. Top with Nutmeg.
| drinkware   = [[Mug]]

A '''Tom and Jerry''' is a traditional [[Christmas and holiday season|Christmas-time]] cocktail in the United States, sometimes attributed to British writer and [[boxing]] journalist [[Pierce Egan]]<ref>https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1014400-tom-and-jerry "It...is frequently (though not definitively) credited to Pierce Egan, the English chronicler of sports and popular culture." Egan was the author of the 1821 novel ''[[Life in London (novel)|Life in London; or, the Day and Night Scenes of Jerry Hawthorn, Esq., and his elegant friend, Corinthian Tom]]'', on which the stage play of the same year ''[[Tom and Jerry, or Life in London]]'' was based</ref> in the 1820s. It is a variant of [[eggnog]] with [[brandy]] and [[rum]] added and served hot, usually in a mug or a bowl.

Another method uses egg whites, beaten stiff, with the yolks and sugar folded back in, and optionally vanilla extract added. A few spoonfuls are added to a mug, then hot milk and rum are added, and it is topped with [[nutmeg]]. Pre-made Tom and Jerry batter, typically produced by manufacturers in Wisconsin, Minnesota, the Dakotas, and Montana, is sold in regional supermarkets during the Christmas season.<ref>Faust, Eric, Tom and Jerry batter is seasonally available in the [[Jamestown, New York]], area, where a strong Swedish influence is prominent. [http://heavytable.com/connollys-tom-and-jerry-batter-from-superior-wi/ "Connolly's Tom and Jerry Batter from Superior, WI]," Heavy Table, 2009; See also [https://web.archive.org/web/20100116125129/http://www.wisconsinmade.com/gift-ideas/Mrs-Bowens-Tom-Jerry-Mix-2662.aspx Mrs. Bowen's Tom and Jerry Mix].</ref><ref>Tom and Jerrys are so popular in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, that Bryant's Cocktail Lounge maintains a [https://www.jsonline.com/story/entertainment/2019/11/19/tom-and-jerry-classic-wisconsin-cocktail-especially-holidays/2567846001/ dedicated Tom and Jerry room in December], in which the only possible order is a Tom and Jerry.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-25 |title=Montana Made: City Bar's Tom and Jerrys |url=https://www.kpax.com/community/montana-made/2018/12/25/montana-made-city-bars-tom-and-jerrys/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=KPAX News |language=en}}</ref>

==Name==
The drink's name is a reference to Egan's book, ''[[Life in London (novel)|Life in London]], or The Day and Night Scenes of Jerry Hawthorn Esq. and his Elegant Friend Corinthian Tom'' (1821), and the subsequent stage play ''[[Tom and Jerry, or Life in London]]'' (also 1821). To publicize the book and the play, Egan introduced a variation of eggnog by adding {{convert|1/2|USoz}} of brandy,{{dubious|date=May 2016}} calling it a "Tom and Jerry". The additional fortification helped popularize the drink.<ref name="KPHist">{{Cite web |url=http://www.kitchenproject.com/history/eggnoghistory.htm |title=The History of Egg Nog |last=Block |first=Stephen |website=Food History |publisher=The Kitchen Project |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510040731/http://www.kitchenproject.com/history/eggnoghistory.htm |archive-date=2011-05-10 |access-date=2006-12-16}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|sure=n|reason=random web page making questionable historical assertions without citing any sources.|date=December 2020}}

==In popular culture==
Tom and Jerry was a favorite of President [[Warren G. Harding]], who served it at an annual Christmas party for his closest friends.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Russell |first=Francis |title=The Shadow of Blooming Grove: Warren G. Harding In His Times |publisher=Easton Press |year=1968 |isbn=0-07-054338-0 |page=141 |author-link=Francis Russell (author)}}</ref>

Two later cartoon duos, a short-lived [[Tom and Jerry (Van Beuren)|Tom and Jerry]] from Van Beuren Studios in the 1930s, and [[MGM]]'s better known [[Tom and Jerry|cat and mouse rivalry]] from the 1940s through the 1960s, also bore the name, possibly as a [[play on words]] with the drink or the literary works that inspired it.<ref>{{cite book|last1=McMahon|first1=Seán|last2=O'Donoghue|first2=Jo|title=Brewer's Dictionary of Irish Phrase & Fable|year=2004|publisher=Weidenfeld & Nicolson|location=London|isbn=978-0-304-36334-6|page=799}}</ref>

In the story "[[I Yust Go Nuts at Christmas]]" by [[Harry Stewart]], a man drinks a dozen Tom and Jerrys and is [[hangover|hung over]] for the following day's Christmas dinner.

In the movie "Beyond Tomorrow,1940, RKO Radio Pictures, the story takes place at the Christmas season, and every visitor to the house of the three older gentlemen is offered a "Tom And Jerry" Cocktail.
